regex_correctness_spot_check.concern: BA's proposed iter-2 regex `'systemctl\s+(stop|restart|disable|enable|reload|kill|try-restart|reload-or-restart)(\s+|\b)'` — does it correctly match all variants in AC2.5?
trace: Variant `systemctl kill -s SIGTERM happy-daemon-dev`: matches `systemctl ` + `kill` + ` ` (\s+ branch — the space before `-s`) ✓

Variant `systemctl try-restart happy-daemon-dev`: regex must match `try-restart` as a whole token, NOT `restart` greedily matching from inside `try-restart`. Test: alternation is leftmost-then-longest by default in POSIX BRE/ERE. With `grep -qE`, longest alternative wins — 'try-restart' is longer than 'restart' so it matches as 'try-restart' ✓ (provided the alternatives are listed in the right order or the regex engine prefers longest match). NOTE: GNU grep -E uses POSIX semantics where alternation is leftmost — but the engine handles this case correctly because once it sees `try-`, the only matching alternative is `try-restart` (no other alternative starts with `try`). So actually the order within the group doesn't matter for try-restart vs restart because they don't share a prefix anchor. ✓
Variant `systemctl reload-or-restart happy-daemon-dev`: same reasoning — `reload-or-restart` is a unique alternative; matches as a whole token ✓
Variant `systemctl restart happy-daemon-dev` (preserved from iter 1): matches `systemctl ` + `restart` + ` ` ✓
regex_correctness_spot_check.edge_case_concern: What about `systemctl reload-or-restart` falsely matching just `reload` from inside the longer verb? BA's regex listing includes both `reload` and `reload-or-restart` as separate alternatives — grep -qE will match the LONGEST alternative when the engine uses POSIX longest-match semantics, OR will match the FIRST alternative that succeeds when the engine uses leftmost-first. Either way: if `reload` matches, exit 2 fires anyway (since reload is in the deny set). If `reload-or-restart` matches, exit 2 fires. Either is correct. The block is robust regardless of which alternative wins.
